title: Keeping Yourself Top of Mind
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article argues that staying 'top of mind' with people who control opportunities — clients, senior leaders, prospective partners — meaningfully increases the odds they turn to you when something opens up. It draws an explicit parallel to brand marketing, where recall drives sales and loyalty, and argues the same recall dynamic drives interpersonal opportunity. The piece is practical about method, cautioning that simple check-ins can feel hollow in newer relationships unless paired with something of value, and highlighting asking for advice as an especially effective, non-intrusive way to stay memorable. It closes by framing the tactic as a discipline: a consistent cadence of authentic contact rather than one-off outreach.
points: Staying top of mind functions like brand recall in marketing — people naturally direct opportunities toward whoever occupies their recent thoughts.
Bare check-ins can feel inauthentic in newer relationships unless paired with something of value, like news, congratulations, or useful updates.
Asking for advice or guidance is identified as the single most effective tactic, because it makes the other person feel valued rather than solicited.
The core discipline is consistency of contact over time, not one grand gesture.
quotes: Reminding prospective relationships, clients, and senior leaders that you stand ready to engage with them can substantially increase the odds that they will turn toward you with an opportunity.
In the world of marketing, a brand that is top of mind for consumers enjoys increased sales and customer loyalty.
But checking in lacks authenticity in newer or unestablished relationships unless it is accompanied by something of value.
But pound-for-pound, the best way to stay top of mind is by asking for advice, guidance, help, or instruction.
Even busy and influential people feel more confident, valued, appreciated, and expert when they are asked for their advice, insight, and guidance.
